entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Paul of Burgos (Pablo de Santa María) was a Spanish Jew born in Burgos, Spain, who converted to Christianity and became an influential figure in the medieval Spanish church.

As a key exegete, he produced a Latin translation of the Hebrew Bible, known as the 'Burgos Bible', which played a significant role in shaping Christian theology and biblical interpretation. His scholarly work, 'Contra Judaeos', a response to Jewish criticisms of Christianity, showcases his expertise as a Christian theologian and biblical scholar.

Paul of Burgos's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, influencing Christian thought and biblical scholarship for centuries to come. He is remembered as a prominent figure in the history of the Spanish church and a testament to the complex and dynamic nature of religious identity in medieval Spain.
